The beam

A lamp's rows spreading over the GameBoard on the digital lines of its fan, the phase as colour.

A demonstration world, examples/events/gallery/beam_fan.json, written for this page by examples/events/gallery/make_worlds.py: it is not a registered experiment, no number on this page is a registered result, and nothing here enters the register. The law it runs under is the one engine, unchanged.

The GameBoard

An open plane of 41 x 41 Nodes (z periodic with an extent of 1: a plane). At its centre, Node (20, 20), a lamp of the paid family light (quantum 1: a paid family, its rows cost content), the measured event number 1 of the world file, content 33 554 432 at the clock's rate K = 4 194 304, so its turn is 8 phase steps of the circle N = 64 per self-creation and every unit it releases costs 8 content (E = h f). Its lamp releases one unit per self-creation on each of 48 directions, the primitive in-plane vectors (a, b, 0) with |a| + |b| at most 6: the fan. The faces of the plane are open: a row that leaves clicks on the face detector and is booked as escaped.

a row, coloured by its phase on the circle Z_Nthe lamp (a measured event)

Why this page

The owner asked to see how the beam spreads on the GameBoard: "in our system there is something that spreads, the beam, and there are clicks, nothing else". This page shows the spreading alone. Every row (a message in flight: one point of Node x direction x phase x age x amount x number) follows the digital line of its direction by the flight table, at most one Link per interval; on a heading it crosses 32 Links in 55 intervals, and every direction of the fan keeps the same Euclidean pace, c = 1 / sqrt 3 Links per interval, the norm of the flight operator. The phase a row carries is the record's birth phase u, the wheel value: the lamp's count of births less one, modulo N, the same on every row of the record whatever the lamp's turn (the K finding of 2026-09-20, BEAM_LAW note 37), and no phase per Link is declared. One record is born per interval here, so the hue turns once round the circle over 64 intervals from the front inward: the front, born at u = 0, is red, and the rows born later are yellow, green, blue in turn. The clock's turn, 8 steps per self-creation, is what each unit costs the lamp (E = h f), read in the books.

The moving picture

What to see: the front is round, not an octahedron. The six neighbours of a Node are the vertices of the L1 unit ball (the grey diamond in the plane) and the pace c is the radius of its inscribed sphere (the white circle); a row on a heading and a row on a diagonal reach the circle together, since each direction's line is cut so that no direction outruns c. From the front inward the colour turns once around the circle: the phase, an element of Z_64, drawn as a hue, one value per record. Where the fan's lines are sparse (far out, between neighbouring directions) the Nodes are dark: the rows are on the digital lines and nowhere else; nothing spreads sideways, and no Node holds anything between intervals.
